newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: KEPPEL pays 1.0 bln pesos for Manila bank.
newsitem.headline: KEPPEL pays 1.0 bln pesos for Manila bank.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Friday Singapore's Keppel has finalised its acquisition of the ailing Monte de Piedad and Savings Bank with the payment of one billion pesos.
The one billion pesos will be used as fresh equity for the bank, the Central Bank said.
The Keppel group had also promised to put in 1.1 billion pesos to honour unfunded checks, it said.
Keppel will own 60 percent of the bank and will have as its local partner Vicente Tan, who owned a majority in the bank.
Fidel Bugayong, executive director of Keppel in Manila, told reporters the group will prioritise the rehabilitation of the bank before upgrading it into a commercial bank.
"Keppel will be here for a long time. We're putting behind the force of Keppel in the acquisition of the bank," he said.
He added Keppel would still be open to a tie-up with a local bank since Tan's stake will be diluted to 10 percent in Monte de Piedad.
Keppel had outbid Indonesia's Lippo Bank for the troubled bank.
The deal would give Keppel, which had earlier considered a banking presence here, 31 bank branches in the Philippines.
Keppel had also promised to try to reopen the bank on May 8, a pledge made by Lippo in its bid.
Monte de Piedad was temporarily closed two weeks ago after a run on its deposits following reports it had 1.8 billion pesos worth of uncollected loans extended to tricycle operators and drivers.
Monte de Piedad used to be majority owned by the Archdiocese of Manila. The Church sold its majority stake to Tan in September 1995.
